quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has many turns and curves.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look both ways. Go if no traffic is coming.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You can turn right on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. However, you must give the right of way to pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast on wet roads, your tires cannot remove water from beneath them. Your tires lose grip and the car slides on the water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be obeyed only when other traffic is present.
Must be obeyed only when a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs tell you to yield to trains at railroad crossings. Do not try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: If a collision is unavoidable, you should:

options.text: Hit something that will give way instead of something hard.
Hit something parked instead of something moving toward you.
Hit the side of the vehicle or clip it instead of hitting head-on.

questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a crash, choose the safest option: hit soft objects like bushes, hit something stationary rather than something moving toward you, and make it a sideswipe or glancing blow if possible.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires work less well.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
As you drive slower, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires work less well.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on wet roads, the less able your tires are to clear water. Too much speed causes hydroplaning, where your car slides on water instead of gripping the road.

questions.question: When sharing the road with trucks, remember that they generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than cars do.
Need less time to pass on downhill slopes than cars do.
Need a smaller turning space than cars do.
Need less time to pass on uphill slopes than cars do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than cars do.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are heavy and large, they need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the road ahead is divided by a median or barrier. Stay to the right of the dividing line.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: You are approaching a construction area.

questions.explanation: A solid line on the road edge marks the boundary between the travel lane and shoulder. When the line angles toward the center, the road is becoming narrower ahead.

questions.question: How can you avoid crashes caused by alcohol?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no to a drink by saying, "I'm driving."

questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving crashes is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to enter or exit a highway.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks and obey all signs and signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicycles.

questions.question: You must remove snow and ice from:
questions.explanation: The law requires you to remove all snow and ice from your vehicle before driving. You may face fines if you do not follow this rule.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots often.
Drivers yielding the right of way.
Drivers keeping a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers are going too fast for conditions. Always drive at legal speeds and slow down when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.

questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions per mile, so you must focus fully on driving. Any other task can be dangerous and create a distraction.

questions.question: This sign shows:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: To register a vehicle in New Jersey, you must be age ____ or older.
questions.explanation: You must be at least 17 years old to register a car in New Jersey. You also need proof of identity and proof of ownership.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and tell drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns you to be careful when roads are wet and slippery.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who goes first?

options.text: One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.explanation: All four drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The first driver to arrive goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a sharp right turn coming up on the road.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop, just like a stop sign. These lights are used at dangerous intersections.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in school zones?
questions.explanation: In school zones, the speed limit is 25 mph unless posted differently. Drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: If power steering fails, steering becomes much harder. Slow down and carefully drive to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes dangerous fumes from your vehicle. A leak lets carbon monoxide enter the passenger area. Fix any leaks right away.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Less if you drink beer instead of wine.
Less if you drink wine instead of beer.
Most with hard ciders and mixed drinks.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol affect driving. What matters is how much alcohol you drink, not what type.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check blind spots?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spots every time you move your vehicle—when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: You find a vehicle defect that could make driving unsafe. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have money.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that affects safe driving must be fixed immediately. Do not drive the vehicle until it is repaired.

questions.question: You stop at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks. When can you proceed?

options.text: When you can see all tracks clearly.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
As soon as the train passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see all tracks clearly.
questions.explanation: At a crossing with multiple tracks, wait until you can see down all tracks before crossing. Another train may be coming on a different track.

questions.question: At night, how should you look to reduce glare from oncoming headlights?

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road ahead. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells drivers that a lane is ending. Be ready for traffic to merge safely.

questions.question: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, what does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they are signaling a right turn. Adjust your driving if you are following this vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
Slow down when driving in the rain.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires with good tread and proper air pressure. Slow down when it rains. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop and back up right away.
Drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.explanation: Orange work zone signs mean construction is happening on or near the road. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if possible. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop heavy bleeding. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: After an accident, what should a driver do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of wrecked vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because another car could hit you. Turn off the engines of wrecked vehicles.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather and visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign alerts you to an upcoming traffic signal. Be ready for a yellow light, red light, or cross traffic.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask the driver to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians, even if they cross against a red light or are being careless.

questions.question: A driver entering an interstate from a ramp should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering an interstate from a ramp, yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when you have space.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the dividing line is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same direction. You may cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. You should:

options.text: Move the injured away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured where they are.
Not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless necessary. Moving them incorrectly can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. Apply direct pressure to stop severe bleeding.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they should:

options.text: Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus before starting the engine.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can distract you from driving. Calm down and focus on driving before you start the engine.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk at the bicyclist to let them know you're passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed ahead to pull in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space. Bicyclists have less protection than car drivers. Passing too quickly can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the road edge. You should:

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, gently apply the brakes to slow down. Once at a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not sharply jerk the steering wheel.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers the direction they must drive on a one-way street.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down but don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but don't know where the emergency vehicle is, pull to the right curb and stop. Wait until you are sure it is not headed toward you.
